Meeting Header: 2025-03-12 16:00 PDT | Duration: 42 min | Auto-transcript

Summary (auto): Weekly check-in for Catalyst Labs POC focused on latency tuning. Discussed TTFT regressions on long contexts, streaming chunk vs full-stream, kernel choices and quantization tradeoffs. Action items and next runs agreed.

00:00:05 Emily (Redwood AE): okay everybody thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, we have Raj and Lena from Redwood — this is our 3rd weekly sync on the latency sprint for the Catalyst pilot.
00:00:14 Maya (Catalyst CTO): hey thanks will do a quick round, hope you all are well.
00:00:20 Raj (Redwood SE): quick agenda, run numbers review, root cause for the TTFT bump, try sequence bucketing and two kernel variants, then plan the next run.
00:00:35 Omar (ML Eng): quick context — last week we saw average TTFT go from ~80ms to ~140ms for 8k sequences in streaming mode, but throughput steady for shorter sequences.
00:00:48 Raj (Redwood SE): yeah we pulled the logs — looks like KV cache miss amplification when prefix length increases, plus some kernel path falling back to a slower matmul impl on their instance. I think quantization interplay also changed the kernel selection.
00:01:05 Priya (SRE): quick Q, are we sure it's not a network issue? our MTU is default 1500, keepalives are at 30s.
00:01:15 Raj (Redwood SE): good call, we did a network sanity check; RTTs are fine. The pattern matches CPU-side kernel selection: for certain sequence+batch combos the runtime chooses a fallback kernel that does poor single-token latency. it's subtle.
00:01:30 Maya: can you walk through TTFT definition again? we have a couple stakeholders using different metrics.
00:01:34 Emily: sure — for this POC we define TTFT as time from request acceptance to first token bytes emitted to client. that includes any decode/streaming syscall time and scheduling. we also break out server-side compute vs network vs marshalling.
00:01:50 Omar: and streaming — are we using chunked streaming at 64 tokens or immediate token-by-token flush?
00:01:57 Raj: we had been using a 4-token flush by default to amortize syscall overhead; but that introduces a small delay for the first token if the model chooses to emit only after chunk. that interacts with TTFT measurements.
00:02:10 Priya: in our logs it looked like the first chunk was delayed when sequence length exceeded 2k, which is odd.
00:02:20 Raj: there are two hypotheses: one, the runtime is doing prefix KV cache misses due to context assembly cost; two, the kernel selector chooses a different GEMM path for that sequence length causing a longer critical path for the first token. we saw similar behavior when we changed quant from int8 to q4_0 on another test.
00:02:40 Maya: interesting — did you see differences between hosted and dedicated runs?
00:02:44 Raj: yes, on Redwood Dedicated (our internal reserved pool) the TTFT was consistent; on the customer's preprod cluster with different CUDA driver + different gcc/mkl versions we saw the regression.
00:02:58 Omar: our infra is using driver 535.x and a custom container; we did not mirror the exact Redwood runtime build.
00:03:06 Emily: that's why one of the recommendations is to pin kernel and runtime builds for the POC runs. Raj, can you explain the kernel options you want them to test?
00:03:16 Raj: sure — we want them to try three variants: (A) default kernel selection (auto), (B) force cuBLAS-backed matmul for attention and (C) our optimized fused-kernel path (less tested on their driver but often lower per-token latency). also a variant with sequence bucketing: bin sequences into short/med/long and route to kernels accordingly.
00:03:38 Priya: how invasive is forcing cuBLAS? does it change output determinism?
00:03:43 Raj: minimal functionally; numeric diffs within float tolerances, stable for generation. the main tradeoff is latency and single-token behavior — sometimes cuBLAS gives faster steady throughput but slower TTFT.
00:03:58 Maya: and quantization — are you saying int8 caused the problem?
00:04:02 Raj: not necessarily int8, more that q4_0 vs q8_0 can cause different paths; we saw fallback codepaths for certain kernel sizes when using q4_0 with some kernels, which increased TTFT.
00:04:15 Omar: can you remind us how streaming chunk size interacts? we saw 4-token flush and 1-token flush changes.
00:04:22 Raj: yes, smaller flush reduces first-byte latency but increases syscalls and may expose scheduling jitter; chunking to 2 tokens is often a sweet spot. for long contexts you also want prefix caching to be effective so first token work is minimized.
00:04:36 Emily: quick check — are we measuring TTFT client-side or server-side? small offsets matter.
00:04:41 Priya: client-side with a small proxy; we can change to server-side header if needed.
00:04:46 Raj: for our debugging we recommend server-side span and client-side delta; that'll let us see where the time goes.
00:04:55 Maya: ok let's look at the spreadsheet Raj sent earlier.
00:04:59 Raj: open the perf sheet: link: https://redwood.example.com/pocs/Catalyst/perf-2025-03-10 (auto note: link may be placeholder). Key rows: run A default, run B force cuBLAS, run C fused-kernel, runs with q4_0 vs q8_0, sequence-bucketing run.
00:05:20 Raj: I'm seeing TTFT median 78ms on default for short sequences, 138ms median for 8k sequences on their infra. cuBLAS move bumped TTFT to 160ms for long sequences. fused-kernel dropped it to 72ms on our dedicated tests but on their host it errored intermittently.
00:05:40 Omar: err errored? like crash?
00:05:43 Raj: not crash — timeout/slow path on aten fallback, library symbol mismatch sometimes sends things down a slow code path.
00:05:50 Priya: that sounds like a driver ABI mismatch. we can try aligning container builds to your runtime.
00:05:55 Emily: agreed — action item: Raj to share exact container tags and kernel env knobs.
00:06:00 Raj: yes will do; also I'll add exact gdb logs to show the symbol resolution.
00:06:10 Maya: what's the remediation timeline if we need to move to dedicated? execs want a clear decision point.
00:06:16 Emily: recommended decision point is after the next run (Omar's dedicated 1M token run) — if TTFT remains >120ms for long sequences we propose a short dedicated pilot or fallback routing for long contexts to Redwood Dedicated or lower-latency kernel.
00:06:34 Omar: ok we'll do the run. a couple infra notes: we have autoscaling on and occasionally pods get rescheduled which might affect warm KV cache.
00:06:45 Raj: that could explain cache warmup noise. for the POC we recommend a warmup phase to populate prefix caches before measuring. add a 10k token warmup script.
00:06:58 Priya: will add warmup. question about prefix caching: is there a way to persist KV across requests in your runtime?
00:07:06 Raj: yes we have optional sticky sessions or a prefix-KV store approach. for the POC we suggested sticky sessions pinned by user-id, or explicit preloading of context for batch runs.
00:07:19 Maya: we have concerns about memory on the instance; long prefix caches blow up memory usage.
00:07:24 Raj: understood — that's why sequence bucketing is helpful: long-context requests go to larger instance types or dedicated routing.
00:07:34 Emily: let's talk about measurement methodology — we saw that raw client-side TTFT had outliers from reschedules; suggest using p95 and p50 but filter warmup and schedule events.
00:07:45 Raj: yeah filter system events and compute server-side breakdowns: kernel time, KV assembly, serialization, network.
00:07:52 Omar: question: is there an easy flag in the Redwood SDK to force kernel path or quantization during a run?
00:07:58 Raj: yes, runtime flags exist: --kernel-prefer=<auto|cublas|fused> and --quant-config=q8_0|q4_0, and streaming options --stream-chunk-size=1|2|4. I'll put the exact commands in the sheet.
00:08:15 Priya: also please include env vars for CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and CUDA_DISABLE_TIMING if relevant.
00:08:22 Raj: will include that. quick aside — we noticed that enabling explicit nvtx ranges helped us isolate the kernel latency.
00:08:30 Maya: good to know. any thoughts on serialization overhead? we use a thin proxy that reserializes responses.
00:08:37 Emily: small proxies can add 10–20ms depending on implementation; if you can capture server-side first-byte time we can subtract that out.
00:08:45 Omar: we'll instrument. one more — memory format: do you have a recommendation for KV layout to reduce assembly cost?
00:08:51 Raj: use contiguous packed kv Blobs per user session; avoid per-token memcopies. we'll share a small snippet.
00:08:58 Emily: covering security briefly — Priya raised SSO cert rotation and audit log requirements; we'll follow up in a separate thread.
00:09:05 Priya: noted.
00:09:10 Maya: any blockers we should be aware of?
00:09:13 Raj: main blockers: driver/runtime diff, and sequence-length variance causing kernel selection flips.
00:09:20 Omar: plan for our run — we'll run three configs: default+q8, default+q4_0, fused-kernel+q4_0 with bucketed sequences. run length 1M tokens, warmup 10k, measure p50/p95 TTFT and include server-side spans. we'll attach raw logs.
00:09:40 Raj: perfect. if fused-kernel errors we'll also try forcing cuBLAS to isolate.
00:09:46 Emily: timeline recap: Raj sends commands by Friday (2025-03-14), Catalyst runs by 2025-03-18, we regroup next Wednesday unless results come earlier.
00:09:58 Maya: got it. quick question about streaming policy: is there a recommended default for customer-facing apps?
00:10:04 Raj: for latency-sensitive apps we recommend chunk size 1–2 tokens, with a client-side aggregator if needed to reduce syscalls; for high-throughput batch jobs chunking of 4 or more is okay.
00:10:18 Priya: what about fallback routing? can Redwood route long-context requests to Dedicated automatically?
00:10:24 Emily: yes, request routing rules exist by sequence length threshold; we can demo that in a follow-up.
00:10:30 Maya: one last note — our compliance team asked about audit logs for key events; Priya will loop them in.
00:10:36 Priya: will do.
00:10:40 Emily: ok let's go around quickly on any last clarifying questions.
00:10:45 Omar: no, just capture the exact command lines and we'll run the matrix.
00:10:49 Raj: will do, and I'll add a note about expected failure modes and how to interpret logs.
00:10:55 Maya: thanks all.
00:11:00 Emily: thanks everybody, see you next week — meeting done.
